title: Rising Prices Worry Voters Before a Big US Election
summary:
Americans will vote in the midterm elections on November 3. These elections decide who controls the US Congress. Many voters are worried about prices going up. That is called inflation.

For almost a year, President Donald Trump has told voters not to worry about prices. He has said gas and diesel prices would fall soon. Those prices went up a lot after the war with Iran began.

But polls show many voters are not convinced. On average, more than 70 percent of people in recent polls do not like how Trump has handled inflation, according to Silver Bulletin.

New government numbers showed that prices in September were 3.7 percent higher than a year before. Fuel and clothing went up the most.

Spencer Kimball of Emerson College Polling said everyday costs are what worry voters most. Trump has been visiting states like Alaska, Kansas, Ohio and Texas to help Republicans running for the US Senate.
why_it_matters: When prices rise, families may have to spend more on things like gas and clothes.
